newsitem.title: USA: IMF approves release of some $200 mln for Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: IMF approves release of some $200 mln for Ukraine.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund on Monday approved the release of roughly $200 million in credits for Ukraine in a vote of confidence in the country's economic policies, international monetary sources said.
"The situation looks very good," one source, who declined to be named, said.
The money is being made available under an $867 million stand-by loan agreement struck earlier this year.
The nine-month pact is due to expire in February and Ukraine is seeking a $2.5 to $3 billion, three-year Extended Fund Facility (EFF) credit to replace it.

Monetary sources suggested that IMF approval of Ukraine's request for a new credit may partly hinge on the reception that its ambitious reform and budget plans receive from its left-dominated parliament.

The government's draft budget, agreed with the IMF, forecasts a 1997 deficit of 5.5 percent of gross domestic product -- four percent by Western calculations -- and foresees inflation at 25 percent, down from 40 percent this year.
Monday's IMF meeting came on the eve of a gathering here on Tuesday of donor nations and international institutions to discuss Ukraine's financing needs for 1997.
The World Bank in October estimated that the country would require $1.8 billion in foreign money next year.
European Commission economic director Joly Dixon said last week in Kiev that Ukraine would have to take steps to improve its economy if it hoped to receive further funding from the European Union.
